child_drafts.description_long: On March 18, 2026, the Interior Department held an oil and gas lease sale in the National Petroleum Reserve in Alaska. corrected_draft.title: The Atlantic’s “Unthinkable” Reviewed 50 Moments From Trump’s First Two Years
corrected_draft.description_short: The Atlantic’s 2019 “Unthinkable” package selected 50 incidents from Trump’s first two years, according to contemporaneous reporting.
corrected_draft.description_medium: The Atlantic’s January 14, 2019 “Unthinkable” feature surveyed Trump’s first two years through 50 selected incidents. Editor Adrienne LaFrance said a research team reviewed every day of the period and narrowed hundreds of candidate moments to 50, emphasizing breaks with norms in communication and institutions.
corrected_draft.description_long: The Atlantic introduced “Unthinkable” on January 14, 2019, two years into Donald Trump’s first term. In a contemporaneous Atlantic newsletter, the magazine described it as a catalog of 50 improbable incidents that it considered outlandish or destructive; one featured episode was Trump’s May 9, 2017, firing of FBI Director James Comey. In an interview that day with WBUR’s On Point, series developer and co-editor Adrienne LaFrance explained how the package was assembled. A research team examined every day of Trump’s first two years and initially identified hundreds of moments before editors narrowed the selection to 50. LaFrance said the episodes ranged from small to large and were hard to weigh individually as they happened. Looking back across the period, she saw recurring challenges to norms in Trump’s communications with the press and his treatment of institutions. The project was an editorial review of selected events and their cumulative pattern, not a quantitative measure of how readers perceived democratic risk.
